cards.text: Paul is writing to the believers in Corinth, and he's just spent a whole stretch boasting (2 Corinthians 11:16-12:10). Now he says, "I have become a fool, but you drove me to it." That's me stamping a cookie with my eyes closed because somebody DARED me, then pointing straight at them when it comes out a blob.

cards.question: Paul says the Corinthians drove him to act like a fool. He says they should have ___ him instead.

cards.text: Then Paul brings up some people he calls "super-apostles." If anybody ever called ME a super-stamper, friend, I'd want it carved on my handle right under Dorin.

cards.question: Paul says he is in no way inferior to those super-apostles.

cards.text: Then he adds, "even though I am nothing." Next he points to proof the Corinthians saw for themselves: the marks of a true apostle, performed right among them with great perseverance.

cards.question: Which marks of a true apostle does Paul say were performed among the Corinthians?

cards.text: Then Paul asks them straight up how they were inferior to the other churches. Friend, when somebody asks it like THAT, there's a twist coming.

cards.question: Paul says the only way the Corinthians were inferior to the other churches is that he was not a burden to them.

cards.text: Then he says, "Forgive me this wrong!" I think he's having a little fun here. That's like apologizing to your neighbor for shoveling his driveway.

cards.question: Paul says he's ready to come to the Corinthians a third time, and he still won't be a burden. Why not?

answers.text: He wants them and not their things
He has plenty of money saved up
Titus will cover all his costs

cards.text: Then Paul backs it up with a picture about saving up. Good thing he never saw my savings, friend: three sprinkles and a crumb.

cards.question: Paul says one group shouldn't have to save up for the other. Who does he say should save up for whom?

cards.text: Now THAT I get. Six little cutters, and I'd hand over every chocolate chip in this bakery. And Paul says for the sake of their souls, he'll spend his money.

cards.question: Paul says that for the sake of the Corinthians' souls, he will spend his money and ___.
Paul says he'll spend for the Corinthians, but only grudgingly.

cards.text: Then Paul asks them, "If I love you more, will you love me less?" Oof. That's the friend who helped you move three times asking why he didn't get invited to the housewarming.
Paul's still on the subject of money. He says, "Be that as it may, I was not a burden to you; but crafty as I am, I caught you by trickery."
Then he asks, "Did I exploit you by anyone I sent you?" Go ahead, Corinth, check the books. He'll WAIT.

cards.question: Paul asks if he exploited the Corinthians through anyone he sent. Then he names someone he urged to visit them. Who?
Paul sent Titus to Corinth all by himself.

cards.text: Then Paul asks, "Did Titus exploit you in any way?" I bet he already knows the answer. He's not asking. He's ASKING.

cards.question: Paul asks if he and Titus didn't walk in the same Spirit and follow in the same footsteps. What's his point?

answers.text: Titus acted just like Paul did

cards.text: Then Paul asks, "Have you been thinking all along that we were making a defense to you?" Friend, I've heard that question myself, right after an hour explaining why a batch came out burnt.

cards.question: Paul says, "We speak before God in Christ," and he calls the Corinthians beloved. He says all of this is to ___ the Corinthians.

cards.text: Now Paul gets honest about what he's afraid of: when he comes, he may not find them the way he wishes. That's opening the oven door and holding your breath before you look.

cards.question: Paul also worries the Corinthians may not find him the way they wish.
Paul says he fears what he might find when he comes to Corinth. Which of these is on his list?

cards.text: His full list of what there may be has eight things: quarreling, jealousy, rage, rivalry, slander, gossip, arrogance and disorder. EIGHT worries, and I bet every one of them weighed on him.
And Paul's got one more fear about his next visit. Friend, this one gets personal.

cards.question: Paul is afraid that when he comes again, his God will ___ him before the Corinthians.
Paul says he will be grieved over many who sinned earlier and have not ___.

cards.text: Paul names what they haven't repented of: impurity, sexual immorality and debauchery. Heavy words, friend, and you can hear the grief in every one.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Titus will cover all his costs" names Titus before he appears in the passage (12:18). Stop 2 card 3 later asks who Paul urged to visit, with Titus as the right answer. Because the baker has already seen Titus tied to Paul's visits, Titus becomes the only familiar name among Titus, Timothy and Silas, which hints at the later answer.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Titus shows up (stop 2 card 3's answer, then this card's quote) but no card ever says simply who he is, such as Paul's coworker.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question says Paul asks whether "he and Titus" walked in the same Spirit. Verse 18 says "we," right after mentioning that "our brother" was sent with Titus. The text doesn't say who "we" includes, so the question narrows it to Paul and Titus.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't match the action in the verse. In 12:19, Paul asks the question himself, to say this was never a defense. In the joke, someone asks Papa Dorin the question because he has clearly been defending himself. That reverses the action and suggests Paul really was making excuses.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.
